title: Blues guitar, kazoos and homemade street instruments
summary: Punch describes how kids made cane kazoos and played in guitar, tub and washboard street groups.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Is he related to One Eyed Babe?
No, he ain't no really. His native home is in Natchez, Mississippi. But he left there and he's a young fellow and come here.
Well, how would he play? Would these guys use picks or would they use that thing? No, he's just going friendly. You don't see that very much. No.
They're under that 690 band store. You see? Put them in bands. They used to play by themselves.
Well, now they use a flat thing mostly. I see them.
Put a good suit. Now, what other instruments did they use? Did you ever see any homemade instruments?
Well, I don't know. The boys used to make the kazookas.
Oh, how does that go? Kazookas?

Yeah. Well, you get a cane read, see? And you went to mark you something like a, something like a, a kind of mark you. And you put a piece of, cut a hole in it, you know? And put a piece of silk paper over the hole. And you hold the silk paper, put them in the mark and sing in it. Oh, yeah. And the sound is like, you know it is. Juice hops used to be failing them days, too.
Yeah, juice hops. Just hook it up in the front and play anything else they want.
Did they use that with bands?
Well, no, not with bands. I used to go around the street with guitar and play with them. Guitar, tub, washboard, juice hops, all that used to go.
